The draft also calls Lane R all authoritative-path work while assigning authoritative condition-2 Route C work to Lane P, so some work has no unique lane under that rule; see ADV-D036-02.

However, the lane partition silently misclassifies required Route C work as preview-only, and the statement that conditions 2 and 4 both follow SF-3 attributes condition-4 authority to a clause that governs only condition 2; see ADV-D036-02 and ADV-D036-04.

objections.claim: D-036 contains the D-000-required decision classification and applies the additional rule for a decision that turns on user preference.
objections.evidence: D-000's register format requires a decision type, and clause 5 requires decisions turning on user preference to be marked PREFERENCE-LADEN with an overturn procedure cheaper than the decision. D-036 contains no Decision type field. Its five-step order, the choice to run two lanes, and the rule that Lane R preempts Lane P are not mechanically or uniquely derived from D-001; predecessor D-031 classified the same kind of sequence PREFERENCE-LADEN. Alternatives and an Honesty section do not replace the mandatory classification.
objections.proposedFix: Add 'Decision type: PREFERENCE-LADEN.' State that the five-step order and Lane-R-first arbitration are the preference choices. Retain and evaluate the prospective C-D036 overturn under D-000 clause 5, including why it costs less than making and executing the sequence.

objections.claim: Every scheduled act belongs unambiguously to Lane R or Lane P, so the Lane-R-first preemption rule is executable for the whole sequence.
objections.evidence: Lane R is defined as 'all outstanding authoritative-path work under file 08 and D-001.' D-001 condition 2 explicitly classifies DR-117 as a PREFERENCE-LADEN Route C product decision, and file 08 currently keeps DR-117 OPEN and slice-affecting. D-036 nevertheless puts DR-117/default-install and other required product decisions in 'Lane P — preview work.' Thus the same DR-117 work is authoritative Lane R by the universal definition and Lane P by the numbered schedule. When that work's owner contends, 'Lane R goes first; Lane P waits' cannot decide which incarnation proceeds. Calling all of Lane P preview work also understates that some Lane P decisions are required for authoritative readiness.
objections.proposedFix: Define Lane R narrowly as condition-1 Route A successor work, rather than all authoritative-path work, or explicitly allow dual-purpose work and give it one scheduling identity. Label the condition-2 Route C and other authoritative Lane P acts honestly, then state how the priority rule treats them. Do not silently remove them from the authoritative completion path.

objections.claim: The stated dependencies justify putting every adopted Route B disposition after product decisions, register mechanics, and the DR-105/114 actor-scope route.
objections.evidence: The rationale says step 4 dispositions require 'those product/actor facts.' Adopted D-028 selects DR-005's V10/custody/G19 preview scope and adopted D-029 selects DR-008's evidence/retention integration half. Their coordinator-register entries contain no dependency on parallel-product posture, DR-117/default install, DR-105, DR-114, or their actor join. D-030's scoped TM can use actor-scope facts for doctor, but that does not create the same prerequisite for D-028 and D-029. The count-pinned order therefore delays at least two authorized dispositions behind unrelated work while presenting that delay as dependency-derived.
objections.proposedFix: State dependencies per disposition. Allow D-028 and D-029 disposition authoring to proceed when their own owner/evidence prerequisites permit, or identify concrete source clauses that truly require steps 1 through 3 first. If only D-030 depends on actor-scope resolution, gate D-030 alone rather than all of step 4.

objections.claim: The sentence 'Condition 2/4 follow D-001 SF-3' accurately cites D-001's governing rule for both readiness conditions.
objections.evidence: D-001 SF-3 is the new-row rule for condition 2: it says condition 2's quantifier is evaluated over the live register and that adding a row requires a reviewed register-content decision. D-001 treats condition 4 separately; its required gate set is fixed after D-002 selects the slice. SF-3 does not govern condition 4. The slash construction falsely extends one named rule to a second condition and makes it unclear whether D-036 is attempting to alter the gate-set process.
objections.proposedFix: Say condition 2 follows D-001 SF-3. Cite D-001's condition-4 text and D-002's adopted required-gate set separately for condition 4. State expressly that D-036 changes neither set.
